issues: No sign of getting around the measurement. There is no file or network access and no pasted coordinates. All randomness comes from the seeded rng.

Recomputed z: (2.9356 - 2.9370) / (0.0034 * sqrt(1/1 + 1/2)) = -0.0014 / 0.00416 = -0.34. The reported -0.326 fits this once you allow for the 4-decimal rounding of the adjusted values. The candidate is worse than the incumbent by about 0.3 sd, which is within noise. Reject is the right call.

Possible correctness concern (not a veto): the diff does not show what `best` holds. If best[0] is a score rather than the (n, 2) centre array, then `best[0] + rng.normal(0, WARM_SD, (n, 2))` broadcasts a scalar. The warm starts would all sit near ~2.93, far outside the unit square. The harness still checks every packing exactly, so the measured loss stays valid either way. Please confirm that best[0] is the centres array.

Design note: when best is not None, every restart in the HOP_START phase becomes a small perturbation of the incumbent best. That removes the random-restart diversity the phase was meant to give. The later basin-hopping phase (HOP_SD = 0.04) already does local perturbation, so the change mostly duplicates it.
The candidate has only 1 run, and the 2-run incumbent mean (2.9370) equals the best published value. A replicate of the candidate is not worth a slot.
